utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, sit down. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having swelling in my legs and feet since a month ago. Also general body discomfort is there, feeling very tired all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is there puffiness around your eyes also, especially in the morning? Any reduction in urine output?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, eyes are puffy every morning. Urine is also less, and it looks foamy and dark weekly or so I notice it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Before coming here, did you try any treatment? Any local doctor or anyone else you consulted?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. I went to a local compounder near our site. He gave me some pain tablets and said it is just body swelling from hard work. I was taking those for one week but no improvement. I also had tonsillitis problem around 2025 January which I treated on my own with some syrup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That compounder may have made things worse. Unnecessary pain tablets can damage the kidneys. Do you have any history of high blood pressure or asthma?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have high blood pressure for 10 years but I take tablets rarely. No asthma.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any exposure at work — like mine dust, chemicals, or heavy metals? Construction workers sometimes get kidney problems from such exposures.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work near a mine construction site doctor, lot of dust and chemicals. Also recently a family member was sick at home with some fever, and I also had fever after a mosquito bite about six weeks back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain in your lower back or abdomen? Some patients get pain near the ovaries region or lower abdomen with kidney problems.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, there is some dull aching in my lower back doctor, constant and dull. No specific pain near ovaries area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any other medicines currently? Anything for mood or anxiety — like sertraline or escitalopram?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like sertraline or escitalopram. I only take BP tablet rarely, that too only when my head is paining badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all your symptoms — swelling in legs, foamy urine, puffiness around eyes, uncontrolled high blood pressure, and your exposure history — I suspect you have chronic kidney disease, possibly worsened by the self-medication and overuse of pain tablets.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Kidney disease doctor? That sounds serious. What tests are needed?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a serum creatinine, blood urea, urine routine microscopy, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, and a kidney ultrasound. Also CBC and dengue serology given that mosquito bite history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will get all done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing amlodipine 5 mg once daily for your high blood pressure, and furosemide 20 mg once daily to reduce the swelling. Stop all pain tablets immediately — no ibuprofen or diclofenac at all.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any food restrictions? And what about my body discomfort — is that related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the body discomfort is related to chronic kidney disease. Reduce mine dust and chemical exposure at work immediately. Avoid high-protein foods, reduce salt intake, drink only 1 to 1.5 litres of water per day till kidney ultrasound results come. And please take BP medicines regularly, not rarely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, never go to unqualified compounders again. The pain tablets they gave you have damaged your kidneys further. Your tonsillitis episode in 2025 that went untreated properly may also have triggered some kidney inflammation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me do a teach-back. Can you tell me — what medicines are you taking and what are you stopping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will take amlodipine once daily and furosemide once daily. I will stop all pain tablets — no ibuprofen or diclofenac. I will reduce salt and chemicals at mine site, and come back after serum creatinine and all tests are done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good, that is exactly correct. One more thing — if swelling in legs or face increases suddenly, or you get breathlessness or chest pain, go to emergency immediately. Follow up with me in one week with all reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, come in, come in. Please have a seat.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. My family is dragging me here, I told them I am perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What is your main work? And what exactly is the family worried about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a fisherman, doctor. They say my sugar is out of control and my weight gain is too much, but I read on the internet that these things settle on their own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you getting any fatigue, excessive thirst, or frequent urination?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, frequent urination is there, happening twice a week at night mostly. And I have fatigue once a day by evening. I thought it was just from fishing work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any chest pain or breathlessness? Any cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, there is some sharp pain in my chest a week ago. And cough is there, it is productive, happening more often lately. Doctor, I read on internet that sharp pain in chest is just gas trouble.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is not always the case. Do you have any history of TB or any lung problem before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had TB last summer. Took treatment for some months. Also had some surgery and after surgery I had this burning pain in my abdomen, but that settled.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any asbestos exposure at the docks or boat repair yards?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, when I work at the old boat yard there is asbestos in those old boats. Many years of that. But on the internet people say one or two years of exposure is nothing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or drink?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I am smoking a pack a day, and I drink on weekends with friends at the dock.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently for your diabetes, thyroid, or high cholesterol? Are you missing doses?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I am missing doses doctor, I will not lie. I read online that entecavir and ribavirin I was given for my liver problem — people say these have too many side effects so I stopped. Also I stopped my eye drops for the eye pressure problem. Doctor said take it once a day but I forget.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This is concerning. Based on your history of TB, asbestos exposure, smoking a pack a day, and this productive cough with uncontrolled diabetes and hypothyroidism, I am suspecting a combination of metabolic syndrome along with early lung disease.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I searched online and it said metabolic syndrome is very common in fishermen due to diet — is that why? And is hypothyroidism connected to my weight gain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, absolutely, hypothyroidism does contribute to weight gain and fatigue. And missing your medicines is making your diabetes and high cholesterol much worse. The internet is not your doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a TMT to check your heart given the sharp pain in your chest. We will also do a DEXA scan to check your bone density because long-term diabetes affects bones. And a temperature check today as I suspect low-grade fever with that productive cough.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the internet says ribavirin should not be combined with certain tablets — should I restart it or not?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, restart ribavirin and entecavir as prescribed, do not stop on your own. Also restart your eye drops once a day without fail. I am additionally prescribing metformin for your diabetes and levothyroxine for your thyroid.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And please stop smoking immediately — with TB history and asbestos exposure, your lungs are already at very high risk. Reduce drinking also, especially while on ribavirin and entecavir.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also forgot to mention — my feet are paining with a burning pain at night more often lately. Is that also the sugar?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, that burning pain in your feet is likely diabetic neuropathy. We will get a HbA1c done and a nerve conduction study. Please come back in two weeks with all your reports — and this time, no internet diagnosis, only what I tell you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please have a seat. What brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I came for second opinion only. Another doctor was telling me something about operation but I am not sure. I have been having swelling near my groin area for a year now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the swelling soft or hard to touch? And does it come out when you strain or cough?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it comes out when I am straining or lifting. It goes back in when I lie down. The pain is there all the time near my groin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding from bottom or piles complaint also? Some patients have both together.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, actually yes, doctor. There is some bleeding from bottom also, once a week or so. I did not want to mention. And the stool is thin sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good you told me. Any abscess or discharge near the anal area? Any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nothing like fever or discharge. Just the bleeding and pain in the bottom area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any other health conditions? What about sugar problem or knee pain or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor yes, I have sugar problem for a year only, and knee pain is also there. And I have epilepsy since many years and also depression history. I am on medicines for those.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any prostate problem or urine difficulty? And what medicines are you currently taking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor they checked my prostate before, was some mild enlargement they said. For gas trouble I was on pantoprazole but I stopped it on my own last month and started some other tablet from medical shop. I am also taking antiepileptic tablets and antidepressant.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not stop pantoprazole on your own without consulting. Now, do you drink alcohol? I want you to be honest with me.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, doctor, yes, I do take alcohol for 30 years. Only 2 drinks a week now though, doctor. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about smoking? And any exposure to pet dander at home? Sometimes we see allergic reactions causing skin rash or breathing problems in elderly patients.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no smoking. No pets at home. But my grandson was saying someone at school had some infection recently. I do visit him every morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Did the first doctor do any tests like T3 or KFT? Or any colonoscopy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He had asked for KFT and T3 but I have not done them yet doctor. I came here first to take your opinion. He also mentioned ultrasound abdomen for checking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, you have an inguinal hernia on the groin side, and the bleeding with thin stool suggests internal piles, possibly grade two. The prostate enlargement should also be monitored carefully.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is operation necessary? I am scared because of my epilepsy and all. Can it be managed with medicines only?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The inguinal hernia will need surgical repair eventually, but we can plan it properly after your KFT, T3, and ECG are done. For the piles, we will first try conservative management. Your epilepsy medicines need to be coordinated with the surgeon before any anaesthesia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting pantoprazole every morning before food. Also prescribing sitz bath and micronized purified flavonoid fraction tablets for the piles, and glucosamine for your knee pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: What should I avoid doctor? Any food restrictions? And what about my alcohol intake?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop alcohol completely, especially because of your depression history and prostate issue. Avoid constipation — take high fibre diet, drink plenty of water. Do not lift heavy weights as it will worsen the inguinal hernia. And never stop your antiepileptic tablets on your own.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will follow your advice and do the tests soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. So this is the little one? What is your name, beta?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: His name is Arjun, doctor. I am his mother. We are sorry we did not come for so long.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is okay, but it has been many months. What problem is he having now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, recently he is saying his chest is paining and his heart is going very fast, like dhad-dhad. I got scared so I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, the chest pain and the fast heartbeat — is it happening all the time or only sometimes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is happening all the time doctor, almost every few hours. And two days ago he also said his temple was paining very badly, here on the side of his head.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any dizziness or fainting also? Did he fall down at any point?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, one time he felt like the room was spinning. He did not fall but he had to sit down. And he is sweating a lot also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Last time we had checked his blood pressure and it was high. Was he taking his medicines regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor honestly no, he was not taking regularly. I used to forget and he also used to say the tablet is bitter. So we skipped many days, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me check him now. Arjun, does it pain here on the chest? Does your elbow or arm also pain when the chest is paining?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, he said the elbow also hurts once in a while when the chest pain is bad. I did not know that was related.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any family history of bleeding disorders, jaundice, or rheumatoid arthritis in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no doctor, nothing like that I know of. His grandfather has sugar problem but that is all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does Arjun drink a lot of caffeine — cola drinks, energy drinks, tea?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, he drinks cold drinks and packaged juice once in a while but at school sometimes more. And he has a very sedentary lifestyle — he sits and plays on tablet all day, no outdoor playing at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent hospital visit for any infection or illness? And any contact with dogs or other animals?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We had one hospital visit last month for fever. And yes, our neighbor has dogs, he plays with them all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, looking at everything — the chest pain, palpitations, headache at the temple, and the missed medicines — this child has hypertensive urgency with possible cardiac arrhythmia. His blood pressure right now is very high and needs to be controlled urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, hyper — what is that? Is it dangerous? What does that mean for a child?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It means the pressure of blood in his body is too high, like a pipe with too much pressure. Because he missed his medicines, it has gone up again and is causing the chest pain, fast heartbeat, and headache at the temple.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing amlodipine 2.5 mg once a day and atenolol 25 mg half tablet in the morning. Do not miss even one dose. Also giving aspirin low dose for now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop all caffeine — no cold drinks, no packaged juice. He must not have a sedentary lifestyle anymore. Light walking every day is must. No dogs contact until we rule out any infection trigger.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am also ordering ECG, echocardiogram, complete blood count, and renal function test today. We need to check why a child this age is having such persistently high blood pressure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I promise we will not miss medicines this time. We will do all the tests two days ago itself I was planning to come — I wish I had come sooner. Thank you doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about after the hospital stay.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, umm, I am feeling a little better now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: So tell me, how have things been since discharge? Any new complaints or are the old ones frequently returning?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, the gastritis is still there but it is less frequent now. And since morning I am having a bad headache.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gastritis — is the feeling burning type, same as before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, burning in the stomach area, especially after eating. I am also noticing my stools are thin and sometimes green, which is worrying me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Now regarding your liquor intake — are you still drinking or have you stopped?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I have never fully stopped, I am being honest. I take it occasionally now, maybe rarely in a week, not like before.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must understand that even small amounts of liquor is putting heavy load on your liver, especially with your history. Do you have any fumes exposure at your shop?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, there is some fumes from paint and varnish products we keep in the shop. I have been still going to work despite the hospitalization.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Now let me review — you had a hepatitis diagnosis in 2021, correct? And your rheumatoid arthritis and hypertension — are those being managed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor. The rheumatoid arthritis medicines I stopped two months ago because of all the hospital visits. The hypertension tablets I am taking sometimes only, not regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you given heparin during the hospital stay? And are you currently on sertraline for your mood?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they gave heparin in the hospital. The sertraline was started two months ago only, I am taking it but very shy to tell anyone at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is completely fine, no need to be shy about it. I also heard you are caring for a sick family member right now — that must be adding a lot of stress?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my wife has been unwell, so I am managing the shop and home together. Umm, I think the headache and gastritis are getting worse because of no rest.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We did a blood test last visit. I am also checking your heart rate now — it seems slightly elevated. Did you take any acetaminophen for the headache today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I took two tablets of acetaminophen since morning but the headache is still there only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all the findings — the burning in the stomach, thin and green stools, ongoing liquor use, and the background of hepatitis — this is a case of alcoholic gastritis with possible liver involvement and stress-induced headache.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the liver in serious danger? Umm, I am scared.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The liver is under strain right now. We will repeat the blood test including liver function, and monitor your heart rate closely. The most important thing is zero liquor — even occasionally is harmful in your condition.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a proper course — continue sertraline as it is, do never stop it suddenly. For gastritis I am adding a proton pump inhibitor, and for the headache avoid acetaminophen excess since your liver is already stressed — I am writing a safer alternative. Also restart your rheumatoid arthritis medicines as before.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the fumes at shop — should I be worried about those also for the liver?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Mr. Ramesh, it has been quite some time. Where did you disappear to?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor, life got busy. I am here now only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You were supposed to come back many years of follow-up pending now. What symptoms are troubling you currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having body pain every other day and some kind of churning feeling in my epigastric region. Also time ago I started getting this tremor in my hands.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any fever? Have you had chills or headache also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, fever is coming daily in the evenings. The season change is making everything worse I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any rash on skin? Nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The upper part of my stomach feels very unsettled. No rash as such, but my hands feel numb every other day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You have a history of stroke and past surgery, correct? Were you continuing any medicines after that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I was on tenofovir doctor, but I stopped time ago. I also had ear drops prescribed for that ear infection but I used it only a few days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Why did you stop the medications? No one told you to stop, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I felt better so I stopped. Also the cost was becoming high.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? Be honest with me please.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, just rarely doctor... maybe a little more during festivals. I also do yoga 1 hour daily so it balances out, no?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is not how it works. Any smoke exposure at home or from your own habit?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I do not smoke. My neighbour smokes near the window, some smoke comes in but I cannot help that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain in the pelvis area? Any loose motion or blood in stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is some ache in the pelvis also, yes. No blood in stool but motion is irregular.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at the fever pattern, body pain, churning in the epigastric region, and seasonal onset, this presentation is suggestive of typhoid. The tremor and numb sensation could be related to your stopped tenofovir and nutritional deficiency.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? I was also worried it could be dengue.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We cannot rule out dengue without tests. I am ordering vitamin B12 levels and bilirubin also since your epigastric region symptoms and alcohol intake worry me for liver involvement.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am restarting your tenofovir immediately. I am also prescribing a short course of prednisolone for the inflammation and tremor, and the ear drops must be completed as instructed this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can I continue my yoga during this time?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light yoga is fine but reduce to 1 hour daily only, and strictly no alcohol as it will worsen the liver damage and interact badly with prednisolone. Do not miss follow-up this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will be regular from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, welcome back. Please sit down, how are you feeling today after the discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Umm, I am mildly better but still feeling nauseous often and there is some gas trouble in my stomach also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Are you itching anywhere or having any rash on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The rash on my arms has gone down mostly, but my mouth feels dry and slightly swollen inside constantly, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain or stiffness in your knee or any other joint?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, my right knee is paining three times a week, especially after I come back from the construction site.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have a history of tuberculosis or osteoporosis? I see something was noted in your discharge summary.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had tuberculosis back in 2022, and the doctor had told me about early osteoporosis also a month ago when I did the bone scan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Were you prescribed any medicines at discharge? Are you currently taking them all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: They gave me albuterol inhaler for the breathing, doctor. But I am also taking some herbal medicine that my neighbour suggested for the swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please do not mix herbal medicine with your albuterol without asking me — it can cause a bad reaction, especially with your allergy history.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been exposed to birds or any animal at home or at the worksite recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there are birds — pigeons — near our worksite. I have been working there for 20 years almost.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you go to the gym or do any heavy physical activity? And do you take any opioids for pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I do go to the gym on weekends doctor. And I have been taking opioids socially — not regularly — but for 20 years on and off.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you having any breathlessness or cough when exposed to dust or the birds?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cough starts often and my chest feels tight whenever I am near those areas. Also I am fasting for religious reasons since last week, so eating very less.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your birds exposure, the breathlessness, cough, rash, and swelling in the mouth, this looks like hypersensitivity pneumonitis with an allergic reaction — triggered largely by bird droppings and dust at the site.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? Will my knee pain and the gas also get better with treatment?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, once we control the allergic response and you stay away from birds and heavy dust, most symptoms including the gas and knee discomfort should ease. Fasting can worsen the feeling nauseous so please sip water constantly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing cetirizine for the itching and swelling, pantoprazole for the gas and feeling nauseous, and continue your albuterol inhaler as needed. Stop the herbal medicine immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I take anything for my knee pain doctor? It is mild but bothering me at work.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Given your osteoporosis, I will add calcium carbonate and vitamin D3 supplements. For the knee pain, apply a diclofenac gel locally — do not take oral pain tablets with your current medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to do a follow-up AST test to check your liver since you have been taking opioids, and also a BP check today before you leave.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will get those done. Should I avoid the gym on weekends for now? And the feeling nauseous is mild only after I eat something, not otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, long time no see! How are you doing, my friend? Still driving your auto?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, same old life. But this time I am here for that insurance paper work only, they are asking for full medical report.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, of course. But tell me also, how is the body feeling? Any new fatigue or pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, fatigue is there all the time. Even after sitting in the auto for just one hour, I feel completely drained.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And that old hernia trouble near the abdomen? Is the bulging still coming when you strain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Haan doctor, it is there only. Sharp pain is coming several times in the day when I am pushing or lifting anything heavy.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And those piles — any bleeding from the bottom or pain during motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Little bit bleeding is there sometimes, and the abscess near the anal area that was drained last time — that place is still paining doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Do you have history of high blood pressure, TB, or cancer in the family? For the insurance form I need to document all this.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, no cancer in family. High blood pressure my father had. TB I myself had before the tests only, remember? That time you had sent me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes yes, I remember. And are you chewing tobacco still? What about marijuana?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, chewing tobacco I am still doing doctor, I know it is bad. Marijuana I stopped. But cigarettes — I am taking 10 cigarettes a day minimum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And food habits? Are you eating properly or still on junk food only?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor what to do, on road the whole day — junk food only is available. Proper food I cannot afford also, financial condition is very tight these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Are you taking any medicines currently? Before the tests did you take anything? What about the iron supplements I had prescribed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not taking doctor, iron supplements I stopped because I could not afford buying them every month. No other medicine also I am taking.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: See, based on everything — your hernia, piles, and that abscess history — these are three separate surgical problems. The fatigue is likely from anaemia because of the bleeding and poor diet.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for insurance they are also asking about my hospital visit history and any ongoing treatment. Can you put all that in the report?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I will document the hospital visit records, the surgical history of abscess drainage, and current hernia and piles status. We also need to run sonography of the abdomen and LFT for complete documentation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the sonography and LFT — how much will it cost? I am telling you honestly, I have very little money right now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Don't worry, I will write government hospital referral so cost will be very less. And about the cough — is there any productive cough or is it clear discharge only? Given your TB history I want to rule out any recurrence.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, little cough is there, the sputum is clear and sometimes productive in the morning. Chest is also feeling heavy sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I am restarting your iron supplements — please take them regularly. I am also prescribing sitz bath treatment and xylocaine ointment for the anal area pain. For the hernia we need surgical opinion, I will write referral letter.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor the sharp pain in abdomen is really troubling me several times in the day. Can something be done without operation? Operation I cannot afford at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation completely. But delaying hernia surgery can cause serious complications. Meanwhile, stop chewing tobacco and reduce junk food — these are making the anaemia and abscess healing worse. I will attach all the documentation for your insurance and also write a letter recommending free surgery under government scheme.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. I am an IT person, doing night shifts, so my schedule is completely off. I came for a refill and also to show this rash on my chest area near the sternum.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me have a look. How long has this rash been there, and is there any itching also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started a couple of months back, doctor. There is itching happening more often lately, and the rash is spreading a little on my lower back also now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you travel anywhere recently, like a rural or congested area? Any exposure to contaminated food or unhygienic surroundings?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went to a village stay program a couple of months ago. The food and water there were not so clean, definitely some contaminated food must have been taken. And the area had a lot of heat and humidity, which I am not used to.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any discharge from the rash, or any scaling or ring-shaped patches on the skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there are ring-shaped patches, and a bit of scaling. Also my lower back is red and flaky near the edges.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what I am seeing, this looks like a clear case of fungal infection — specifically tinea corporis. The heat and moisture from your travel, combined with night shift sweating, have made things worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so it is a fungal infection only? Is that why the itching on my sternum is so bad after every meal especially when I sweat?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Exactly. Sweating after eating and sitting long hours at your desk is worsening the fungal infection. Also, cold weather in your air-conditioned office can cause dryness that makes the rash crack and itch more. You need to keep the area dry and clean.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing you clotrimazole cream to apply on the chest and lower back patches twice a day, and fluconazole tablet once a week for four weeks. Also continuing your ranitidine refill as before for your gastric trouble.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the ranitidine — I have been on it since 2021. My previous doctor started it. Is it still okay to continue?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, ranitidine is fine for now for your acidity. But since you have been on it since 2021, we should monitor. Are you still having heartburn or acidity after every meal?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, the acidity is after every meal, and I drink a lot of coffee also during night shift to stay awake. I have been drinking coffee since I was young, so it is a habit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you exercise at all? And do you drink alcohol — how many drinks per day roughly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, exercise is almost zero doctor with these night shifts. And I take around 3 beers a day to wind down after shift. I know it is not good.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That 3 beers a day combined with coffee is directly worsening your acidity and also suppressing your immunity, which is making the fungal infection persist. You must cut down alcohol and coffee, and start some exercise even if short walks.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, you mentioned PSA test last time in 2022 — should I repeat it now? I had some urinary frequency also off and on.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you remembered. Since the last PSA test was done in 2022 and you are now reporting urinary frequency, yes we should repeat it. I will also add a urine routine examination and KFT to the order.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Also sometimes I get lower back pain on my lower back region, which comes more often lately, and I thought it may be from sitting long hours.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, long hours of sitting at the desk causes lower back pain. The cold weather from air conditioning also stiffens the lower back muscles. Start exercise and take short breaks every hour from your desk.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me do a quick teach-back — can you tell me how you will use the clotrimazole cream and the fluconazole tablet that I just prescribed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sure doctor — clotrimazole cream I will apply on the chest near the sternum and on the lower back rash twice a day, and fluconazole I will take once a week for four weeks. I will also reduce coffee and alcohol, try to exercise a little, and come back if the itching does not reduce.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Perfect, you have got it right. Also make sure to do the PSA test, urine routine examination, and KFT this week, and come back in three weeks. If the rash spreads further or the itching becomes unbearable, come earlier.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in. Please have a seat. What is your name and how old are you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Arjun. Sixteen years old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Arjun, you have come for pre-operative clearance today, correct? What surgery is planned?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor. Today. Some kidney procedure. My parents arranged it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you having any swelling — on your face, legs, or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, on my legs mainly. Once in a while my face also gets puffy in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bruising on your skin without any injury? Or spasms in your legs or arms?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, bruising happens hardly ever. Spasms in my legs happen once a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cough? Is the cough producing any sputum — is it thick or mucus-like?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: A little cough. It is dull and mucus is there sometimes. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of jaundice, pneumonia, or any gallbladder issue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, jaundice when I was small, doctor. No pneumonia or gallbladder issue that I know of.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about exposure to pollen or animal hair — any allergic reactions or breathing difficulty?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, nothing like that. We do not have pets at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any medicines currently — any OTC medicine like painkillers, or do you use an albuterol inhaler for breathing?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I took some OTC medicine for headache last month. No albuterol. I was told to stop everything before surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Also, I heard you are fasting for religious reasons right now. How long have you been fasting? Any dizziness or weakness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fasting today only, since morning. Some weakness, but it is okay.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does anyone in your family drink alcohol? I ask because kidney disease can sometimes run in families with certain habits. What about you — do you ever drink?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, only socially. Maybe 2 drinks a week, after meals sometimes. Not regularly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. We need to check your blood sugar given the fasting and your creatinine levels. Has any doctor mentioned TB at any point?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No, never. No one mentioned TB.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Arjun. Based on the swelling, creatinine elevation, and your symptoms, this is consistent with chronic kidney disease. We will proceed with pre-operative workup.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing furosemide for the swelling, and calcium carbonate tablets for the spasms. Please take them once a week review as instructed after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, avoid all pollen and animal hair exposure, stop alcohol completely, and do not take any OTC medicine without asking us first. The blood sugar result must come before we clear you for surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Oh, it is you! Long time no see — where have you been hiding? I was wondering what happened.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I know, I know, doctor! I am so sorry. Work at the stall was too hectic and then I was fasting for the religious season, so I kept missing appointments.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, no scolding today, but you must be regular. Now tell me, how are the periods these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, that is the main problem. In January they had almost stopped, and then this morning I noticed some discharge, which is why I finally came in.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the discharge happening multiple times a day, or just occasionally?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, multiple times a day doctor. It is yellowish and there is some itching also in the belly area, lower side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any pain near the uterus region, like lower belly cramping?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dull ache is there monthly around period time, but it gets better after two or three days on its own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: When we last met back in 2023, your ultrasound had shown cysts. Have you been doing any exercise as I had recommended?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, nope doctor, honestly no time. Standing at the stall daily is all the moving I do. Exercise properly — don't think so I have managed even once.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about your food and habits? Do you drink alcohol or use cannabis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I will be honest — I do take alcohol, around 3 beers a day after stall hours. And cannabis sometimes on weekends to unwind. I know it is not good.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any pets at home, or do you work near a construction site? I am asking because sometimes environmental exposure can affect hormones.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, my stall is right next to a construction site, dust is everywhere. And yes, we have two cats at home, so pets are present.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you been taking the metformin I had prescribed earlier for the PCOS?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I stopped after a few months doctor, because I felt better. I also had irregular periods since teenage years but I never followed up properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, so based on everything — the irregular cycles, cysts on the previous ultrasound, discharge, and your lifestyle — this is a flare-up of PCOS with a secondary vaginal infection. We need to address both.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, can the alcohol and cannabis be making the PCOS worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely yes — alcohol especially at 3 beers a day can disturb your insulin and hormone levels badly, directly affecting the uterus and worsening the cysts.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing metformin 500 mg twice daily again, fluconazole for the vaginal infection, and clindamycin cream to apply locally — please do not skip this time.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: And doctor, what should I do about food while fasting? I do not want the medicines to cause nausea or acidity on an empty stomach.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Take metformin only after you break your fast — never on empty stomach, it will cause nausea. Also please start at least 30 minutes of exercise — walking is enough — daily.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Cut down the alcohol completely while on metformin — combining them can cause dizziness and even hypoglycaemia. And reduce the cannabis too, it is not helping your hormones.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will try my best. Should I do that ultrasound again and any blood test?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes — get a repeat pelvic ultrasound, fasting insulin, and LH/FSH ratio done this week, and come back to me in two weeks without missing, okay? No more disappearing for months!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about so soon after discharge.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thanks doctor. I am still noticing blood in urine every morning and I have burning sensation in my throat for two weeks now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the blood in urine frank red or more of a pinkish tinge? And is the throat burning on and off or constant?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is frank red doctor, only in the morning stream. The throat thing is on and off, mainly after I wake up or after a session at the gym.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Given your asthma history, do you notice any seasonal pattern? Does it get worse in winter or spring?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my asthma definitely flares up seasonally. Every morning in winter I am coughing more and I do get wheezing with exertion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any secondhand smoke exposure at home or gym? And have you been living in or near a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The gym is smoke-free but I visit relatives in a rural area sometimes. There is quite a bit of secondhand smoke there as most of the older men smoke indoors.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about your own smoking habit? Are you still a smoker?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Technically I smoke only socially now, but at the party last weekend I went up to almost a pack a day level. My friends call me a chain smoker when I drink.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Speaking of which, how much alcohol are you consuming? Any mercury exposure through diet or supplements?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I drink alcohol quite heavily on weekends doctor, I will admit. As for mercury, umm, I do eat a lot of large fish like swordfish and tuna post workout. Could that be related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly. Any flank pain or swelling in the legs? Any fever or chills?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I doubt it is fever doctor, I have been checking my temperature regularly. No flank pain either. There is mild puffiness around my eyes every morning though.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right. Were the urine microscopy and kidney function test reports done during your admission available to you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I have them here. The urine microscopy showed red blood cell casts and the kidney function test showed mildly elevated creatinine. The urine culture was negative.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the red blood cell casts, blood in urine, periorbital puffiness, and elevated creatinine, this is IgA nephropathy, also called Berger's disease. The heavy alcohol use and high-mercury fish diet are aggravating factors.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That is what I suspected. Is the asthma connected? I read it is unlikely but I wanted your opinion.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You are right that a direct link is unlikely. However, frequent smoking and the secondhand smoke from your rural visits are keeping your asthma active and may be stressing your kidneys indirectly through chronic hypoxia.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing omega-3 fatty acids capsules twice daily, ramipril five milligrams once daily to protect the kidneys, and continuing your salbutamol inhaler for asthma. I am also adding prednisolone at a low dose for the inflammatory component.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I stop going to the gym completely? And is it safe to keep taking my whey protein supplement?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light exercise is fine but stop heavy straining and lifting for now as it can worsen blood in urine. Stop the whey protein immediately as excess protein load is harmful to already stressed kidneys. Absolutely no alcohol and avoid large fish to cut down mercury intake.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to repeat urine protein-creatinine ratio, serum IgA levels, and a renal biopsy to confirm grade and plan long-term therapy. Your seasonal asthma management should include a pulmonologist review before winter sets in.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will cut down the fish and alcohol. Should I be worried about my kidneys long term given I am only twenty-four?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: With early detection and strict compliance, the prognosis is good. But continued alcohol use, smoking, and mercury exposure can accelerate kidney damage significantly. Follow up in two weeks with the renal function test and urine routine reports.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am okay doctor, thank you. I am here because my operation is scheduled next week and they are asking for pre-operative clearance.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, noted. And what is your occupation? You look like you work with your hands.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a tailor, doctor. I work in a garment factory for more than fifteen years now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Before we proceed to clearance, I can see something on your forehead and arms. Is there any rash or itching bothering you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, that is why I was actually a little nervous to come. I have itching and a rash on my forehead and also on my neck. The itching is very intense.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How long have you had this? And is the rash spreading anywhere else — chest, back, between the fingers?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started around three weeks back doctor. And umm, yes, it has spread a little between my fingers also. I was checking online and I thought it might be some fungal infection, so I delayed coming.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Does the itching happen at any particular time? Is there any burning or discharge from the rash?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The itching is there once a day mainly in the evenings after work. No discharge doctor, but there is some redness and scaling also. I read online it looks exactly like ringworm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And you work in a factory with many other workers? Any factory chemicals or fabric dyes you are exposed to regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we use lot of synthetic fabric and the dyes also. Whole day I am sitting and cutting and stitching. It is a closed factory, not much air also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of allergies — to medicines, fabric, or food? And any past surgery we should know about?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I had a past surgery for appendicitis around eight years back. And I have some allergies to sulpha drugs, doctor — that is documented. Also I have a old injury on my right knee from an accident.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned the allergies — we will be careful with medicines. Do you smoke or drink? Any such habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, since college only — not heavy at all. And drinking also since I was young, but very occasional, only at functions and all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any stomach pain or discomfort in the epigastric area? Any acidity or heartburn?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, actually I do have some acidity problem. The epigastric area is sometimes uncomfortable after surgery — it started after my appendix operation only. I am taking ranitidine on my own sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any joint pain or aching in the bones? Sometimes with skin infections there can be body ache also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, my bones are fine. No joint pain. Only the skin is bothering me. I was reading online about fungal infection and it said I should apply some antifungal cream — so I tried one from the medical store but no relief.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I have examined the rash on your forehead, neck, and between the fingers. This is a case of dermatophytosis — what you correctly guessed, a fungal infection. The moist closed environment at your factory is likely contributing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ah, so I was right doctor! I read about it online. So what do I do now? Will it affect my operation also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to treat this before the operation. I am prescribing terbinafine tablets once daily and clotrimazole cream to apply on the rash area twice daily. Do not use the over-the-counter cream anymore — it was not the right formulation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please avoid prolonged exposure in the closed factory without ventilation until this clears. Keep the skin dry and clean. We will also do a KOH smear test and routine blood work for pre-operative clearance — your allergies to sulpha drugs are noted and we will ensure the anaesthesia team is informed.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will do as you say. Should I continue the ranitidine also for my epigastric problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ah, Rajendra ji! Good to see you. How is the family? Your son's wedding preparations going on well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: All good doctor saab, very hectic days. The wedding is next month. But today I have come for my quarterly check and also my grandson is not well.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Oh, the little one is unwell? What is happening with him?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He has been having fever and diarrhoea — the stools are watery — couple of days now. He is only four years old.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any vomiting also? And is the fever continuous or going up and down?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, some vomiting also started two days ago. The fever is often coming back, not settling fully. A family member was sick last week with similar complaints, so I think the child caught it from there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of asthma or allergies in the child? And has he been given anything at home for the fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No asthma, but he does have some allergies — some food items. We gave him ibuprofen syrup last night, periodically as needed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, based on the watery diarrhoea, fever, and the family member was sick history, this looks like a viral gastroenteritis. We will manage it with oral rehydration and continue ibuprofen for fever control.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the child, I am prescribing ribavirin in syrup form for the viral load, and continue ibuprofen after meals only. Make sure he is getting plenty of fluids.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Now for myself — I have been feeling uneasy on my right side periodically. Also there is some gas trouble often these days.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The uneasiness on the right side — is it on the back also, or only front? Any tingling sensation on the skin around that area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor — it is going from the right side to the back also. And yes, there is this tingling on the skin there. It is ongoing for a week or so.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has any rash appeared on the skin in that area? And is there a cyst or swelling you can feel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes a small cyst kind of thing I noticed on the skin near the back. No full rash as such yet.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any asbestos exposure during your government service years? You were in public works, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Active exposure for many years yes — there was plenty of asbestos in the old buildings we worked in. But that was long back doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Any cocaine or substance use? I have to ask formally. And how about physical activity these days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Never doctor, no cocaine or anything like that. Physical activity is less these days — wedding planning is tiring. Earlier I used to smoke two packs a day but I stopped five years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The tingling on the skin, the cyst, and the right side to back radiation — this pattern is suggesting early herpes zoster. The stress from wedding preparations may have triggered it.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should we do some test? And what about my blood pressure review — is that ongoing as before?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, BP review is ongoing. We will check your blood pressure reading today and also do a lumbar puncture to rule out any nerve involvement given the tingling pattern. Strong family history of nerve conditions means we should not take chances.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For you, I am prescribing ribavirin antiviral course for the herpes zoster, and continuing losartan for your hypertension. Take losartan after meals as usual.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Any precautions for the gas problem doctor? It is becoming quite troublesome.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid heavy oily food for now, the gas and uneasy feeling on the right side should settle once the herpes zoster is treated. Keep physical activity light — short walks are fine. Come back in two weeks or sooner if the rash spreads on the skin.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello beta, come in, come in. And you must be his father, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. He is my son, he is twelve years old. He is complaining of headache and dizziness for three months now. He did not want to come but I forced him.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, beta tell me yourself — where exactly is the headache? Is it at the forehead or back of the head?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mostly at the back of my head doctor. And sometimes it is very sharp, like it shoots up suddenly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any numbness in your hands or feet? Or any tingling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, almost never is it in the feet, but the hands do get numb sometimes, especially in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any sore throat, fever, or vomiting along with this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: He had sore throat about a week back, doctor, but that went away on its own. No vomiting as such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Father, does anyone at home smoke? Is the child getting exposed to secondhand smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I smoke myself. Two packs a day I have been doing for 10 years. I try not to smoke inside but sometimes I do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And father, you mentioned you work somewhere — what is your occupation? Have you been taking the child near any mine area or factory site?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I work in a coal mine doctor, for three months the boy has been coming to drop me on his cycle in the morning. He waits near the entrance sometimes for a bit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has he been in contact with any sick person recently — like someone with tuberculosis or respiratory infection?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not that I know of doctor. One neighbour had some cough problem but we do not visit them much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has the child been given any medicines at home? Any paracetamol or other tablets on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, we were giving him ibuprofen whenever the sharp pain came. From the medical shop only, no prescription. And he has a history of anxiety disorder — was diagnosed last year.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Let me check his pulse and blood pressure now. Beta, any pain in the abdomen or liver area, meaning right side below the chest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing in the liver side. Just the headache and sometimes dizziness when I stand up fast.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Father, does anyone in the family have joint pain or rheumatoid arthritis? Any autoimmune conditions in family history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife's mother had rheumatoid arthritis doctor. But as for the child, we have ruled out that possibility since he was tested last year and reports were normal. Also, does he wine or anything — no, absolutely not, he is twelve only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on all this — the occupational mine dust exposure, the secondhand smoke, the anxiety disorder background, and the very sharp recurrent headache with dizziness and numbness — this looks like a combination of tension headache with possible early peripheral neuropathy triggered by toxic exposure.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is it serious? What should we do now? Should we stop him from going near the mine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, immediately stop taking the child near the mine. I am prescribing gabapentin in a low paediatric dose for the numbness and sharp pain episodes, along with vitamin B12 supplements. Stop the ibuprofen on your own — that is not safe.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Father, most importantly, please stop smoking inside the house — the secondhand smoke is worsening his headache and dizziness. We will also do a complete blood count and nerve conduction study to check the numbness properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, we will do all the tests. And I will make sure he does not go near the mine anymore. Thank you for explaining everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, please sit down. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am okay doctor, just came for the review after the operation.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right, this is your post-surgery review. Tell me, any pain or discomfort in the abdomen area since we did the procedure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, for six months I had a lot of pain in the lower abdomen, but not anymore doctor, it has settled down mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Any bleeding or discharge from the wound site? Any swelling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: denied, nothing like that doctor. The wound is fine. But sometimes I get sharp pain in the lower abdomen, every other day, especially at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That sharp pain — is it worse at night or also in the daytime?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly worse at night doctor. During the day I am doing my labour work so I am not noticing, but at night it troubles me frequently.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any nausea, vomiting, or loose motion? How is your bowel?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, loose motion is there on and off doctor. And my abdomen feels crampy sometimes. They had told me I have some colitis also, I think.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, the ultrasonography report did show some inflammation. Any history of pneumonia or any lung problem before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: true doctor, I had pneumonia 6-7 months back, around the same time as the pregnancy complication. I was given some antibiotics at that time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any cough or breathlessness now? Any fever?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: denied doctor, no fever, no cough. But I am having knee pain on and off, especially in the calf area also it is paining.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The knee pain — any swelling or redness near the calf? Any history of insect bites recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, I work outside a lot. There is some insect bites happening. One of the children also had some rash — someone at school had spread an infection, they said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you smoke or take liquor?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I take liquor on weekends only. And I smoke 10 cigarettes a day. I also do some physical exercise, 1 hour daily, as part of my labour work only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We should do a BUN test to check your kidney function, and also schedule a follow-up ultrasonography report for the abdomen. Have you been taking any medicines currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was taking some antihistamines for the skin rash from the insect bites, doctor. Otherwise nothing else.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at all your symptoms — the colitis, the sharp pain in the lower abdomen, and the post-operative history — this appears to be a case of post-surgical colitis with secondary bowel inflammation. The knee pain and calf discomfort may be related to the insect bites causing a reactive response.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what should I do about this? Will the colitis go away? I am worried because the sharp pain in abdomen is very troubling at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing amoxicillin for the infection component, and continue antihistamines for the rash and allergic reaction from the bites. Avoid liquor completely till the colitis settles.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please reduce smoking — it is affecting your recovery. No heavy lifting in your labour work for now. Come back after the BUN result and the follow-up scan for proper reassessment of the abdomen.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will do the BUN test and come back for the follow-up. I will try to manage the smoking also. Thank you doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you feeling after the surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor, much better than before, but for six months I am having this yellowish discoloration of my eyes and skin — it is coming and going.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let us start from the beginning. Any fatigue, nausea, or loss of appetite also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, tiredness is there more often lately. Also, some pain near the belly button area, especially after eating.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the pain near the belly button sharp or dull and aching? And any swelling or hardness there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is more dull and aching, doctor. Sometimes also paining in the joints — knee and wrist both. I wanted to ask you about this constipation problem also—

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will come to that. First tell me, any dark urine or pale stools? And how often does the jaundice flare up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, dark urine is there doctor. The jaundice flare happens once a week roughly. And itching on skin also, I forgot to mention.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now let me ask about your history. You had a hernia repair six months ago, correct? Any allergies that were noted before surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, hernia repair was done at district hospital. And yes, I have allergies — to some insect bites, my whole arm swells up whenever that happens.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any exposure to mold at home or fumes at work? As a constable you may be near vehicles or chemicals.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh yes, lots of fumes on traffic duty doctor, almost never can I avoid it. And our old quarters has mold on the walls, especially in rainy season.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, I have to ask directly — you had a history of alcohol use. Are you still drinking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, not anymore the heavy drinking. Now only drinking alcohol on weekends — just one or two. I have cut down a lot, I promise.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about smoking or tobacco? And how much tea are you taking in a day?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking I have stopped, never touch it now. Tea I take too much doctor, maybe five to six cups. And I started walking in the morning as doctor advised after surgery.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you are doing walking. Have you done any recent blood tests? We need your ESR and creatinine levels checked, along with liver function test.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did liver function test last month doctor — bilirubin was high they said. But ESR and creatinine were not done. Also I was given some liver tonic syrup by the previous doctor but I stopped it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the jaundice, fatigue, high bilirubin, and your history of alcohol use, this is a case of alcoholic fatty liver disease with cholestatic jaundice. The joint pains may be a related inflammatory reaction.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this very serious? Will the liver be damaged permanently? I am worried about my job also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. They sent me from the society health camp, said I should get properly checked because my BP was coming high there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right, so let us go through everything carefully. Are you having any chest pain or palpitations — meaning your heart feels like it is beating fast or fluttering?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, for a month I am feeling this beating sensation in my chest, and occasionally there is some chest pain also, but mild only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or nausea along with the chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, nausea is there sometimes doctor, but vomiting — nope, nothing like that has happened.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Now, how long has the BP been high? Has anyone told you before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, over a year they are saying my pressure is on the higher side. I was not taking it seriously, thinking it is just tiredness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any past history of TB or any serious illness before? Any blood transfusion taken at any time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
